Plot Bayesian Residual Q-Q Plots with Credible Simulation Envelopes

Source: R/bayesian_diagnostics.R, R/generics.R
plot_qq.Rd

Evaluates distributional and normality assumptions for endogenous variables in a because model using Randomized Quantile Residuals (Dunn & Smyth 1996) and Posterior Predictive Credible Envelopes (Landwehr et al. 1984).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'because'
plot_qq(object, resp = NULL, ndraws = 250, ...)

plot_qq(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted because model object.

resp

Character vector of response variable names to evaluate. If NULL (the default), all endogenous response variables in the model are plotted and faceted into a multi-panel display. Provide a single variable name (e.g. resp = "Brain") to plot a single variable, or a character vector to select a subset of responses.

ndraws

Integer; number of posterior predictive draws to simulate for the envelope. Defaults to 250.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

A ggplot2 plot object.

Details

Standard Q-Q plots for non-Gaussian or structured models can be misleading because discrete or constrained responses do not follow standard normal error distributions. plot_qq resolves this by computing Randomized Quantile Residuals via the Probability Integral Transform (PIT) against simulated model replications (\(y^{\text{rep}}\)), which follow an exact standard normal distribution under the correct model (Dunn & Smyth 1996; Hartig 2022).

In addition, an empirical simulation envelope is constructed by sorting replicated residuals across posterior predictive draws (Landwehr et al. 1984):

  • The darker blue central band represents the 50% posterior predictive envelope (interquartile range).

  • The lighter blue outer band represents the 95% posterior predictive envelope.

Residual points falling systematically outside the 95% envelope indicate model misspecification, unmodeled skewness, heavy tails, or zero-inflation.

When the model contains multiple equations (as in structural equation models), calling plot_qq(fit) automatically facets across all endogenous response variables.

References

Dunn, P. K., & Smyth, G. K. (1996). Randomized quantile residuals. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 5(3), 236-244.

Landwehr, J. M., Pregibon, D., & Shoemaker, A. C. (1984). Graphical methods for assessing logistic regression models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 79(385), 61-71.

Hartig, F. (2022). DHARMa: Residual Diagnostics for Hierarchical (Multi-Level / Mixed) Regression Models.

Gelman, A., Meng, X. L., & Stern, H. (1996). Posterior predictive assessment of model fitness via realized discrepancies. Statistica Sinica, 733-760.

See also

check_normality, check_model, residuals.because

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Plot Q-Q envelopes for all equations in the SEM
plot_qq(fit_model)

# Plot a specific response variable
plot_qq(fit_model, resp = "Brain")
} # }
